ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity (black) ventral surface with sparse, high-intensity (white) pixel clusters; estimated ratio of 15:1 black to white surface area.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Concentrated high-intensity white mottling at the distal lateral tips of both lobes; discrete, roughly circular white pixel clusters (spots) distributed sporadically across the central and medial black regions of the fluke surface.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Acute V-shaped indentation with a calculated angle of approximately 50 degrees and significant vertical depth relative to the lobe horizontal midline.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Asymmetrical serration profile; left lobe trailing edge features moderate-frequency, low-amplitude irregularities; right lobe trailing edge features high-amplitude, jagged, saw-tooth protrusions and deep indentations.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Convex arc along the visible leading edge tapering into acute, upward-curving lateral tips; trailing edge follows an irregular concave sweep from the notch to the tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Numerous small, high-contrast white circular pixel clusters (0.2-1% of total lobe area) scattered across the dark ventral surface, appearing more concentrated on the lower-right quadrant of the right lobe.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Several distinct, unaligned vertical and diagonal high-contrast linear streaks visible on the medial and lower portions of the right lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Pronounced tissue fraying and textural irregularity at the distal left tip; significant jagged excision (potential trauma mark) on the inner trailing edge of the right lobe near the median notch.
other_distinctive_markers: Unique high-density cluster of white micro-speckles located specifically on the lower mid-section of the left lobe, distinct from the larger scarring patterns.
